Blatant

/BLAH-tunt/ — stress on first syllable, rhymes with tenant · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something blatant is so obvious and out in the open that it cannot be missed or reasonably denied.

The referee somehow missed the blatant push right in front of him.

Worked Example

The student submitted an essay copied word-for-word from Wikipedia — an act of plagiarism so blatant that no one could deny it or explain it away.

Blatant captures not just that the plagiarism occurred, but that it was flagrant and obvious, done without any attempt to hide it. This is more precise than 'obvious' (which could describe subtle things) or 'dishonest' (which is broader and does not emphasize the brazen openness).

How Blatant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

obvious

obvious: easy to see or notice

glaring

glaring: so noticeable it demands your attention

flagrant

flagrant: shockingly open in breaking a rule

Antonyms

subtle

subtle: so slight it is easily missed

inconspicuous

inconspicuous: quiet and unlikely to draw notice

How Strong Is It? — hidden → subtle → obvious → blatant

hidden vs. blatant

hidden vs. blatant: Hidden sits at the opposite end of the scale from blatant: a hidden fault cannot be seen at all, while a blatant one is impossible to miss.

subtle vs. blatant

subtle vs. blatant: Subtle is far weaker than blatant; a subtle hint can easily slip past you, but a blatant act is shamelessly out in the open.

obvious vs. blatant

obvious vs. blatant: Obvious is weaker than blatant: an obvious mistake is easy to notice, while a blatant one is so glaring it seems to dare anyone to deny it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — blatant

Root — blatant: noisy, babbling — a poet's coinage for a loud slander-monster (English coinage (Spenser, 1596; ultimate origin uncertain))

Put it together

Put it together: Spenser invented blatant to describe a monster of loud, wagging tongues, so the word began as 'offensively noisy.' Something blatant still 'shouts' in a figurative sense — it is so loudly obvious that it cannot be missed or reasonably denied.

Use the root in a new word: bleat

Use the root in a new word: bleat: The lost sheep continued to bleat until the whole valley heard it — many scholars think blatant grew out of this same noisy word, which is why blatant things seem to announce themselves loudly.

Strength Check

Word Choice

neutral / everyday

Blatant is best for something so obvious and out-in-the-open that it cannot be reasonably denied or overlooked. Use it when you want to emphasize how flagrantly visible something wrong is. For things that are merely easy to see, 'obvious' is simpler and sufficient.
